_doc: REPEATED PASTES STACK WITH CUMULATIVE OFFSETS — workspace/actions.yaml
paste has required that sentence since it was written, and NEITHER ACTIVE
PORT implemented it: the second paste landed exactly on the first, which is
the single outcome the offset exists to prevent, arrived at by pasting twice
instead of once. Both ports were wrong TOGETHER, so this is a tier-1 spec
violation and not a divergence: the written requirement governs, and JYH
ruled 2026-07-28 'follow the spec' — implement the stacking, do not amend
the sentence.
WHAT `offset` MEANS IN THIS OP. It is the BASE STEP, not the distance
travelled. The Nth consecutive paste of one payload lands at N * offset from
the source, so three pastes at base 24 sit at 24, 48, 72. `paste_in_place`
passes 0 and is outside the run entirely.
COORDINATES. multi_layer.svg is a 96px viewBox, and the SVG codec converts
px to pt (x0.75), so the pasted 16x16 rect at (16,16) is a 12x12 rect at
(12,12) in DOCUMENT space. The offset is applied in document space, on top:
a first paste lands at 12+24 = 36, a second at 12+48 = 60, a third at
12+72 = 84. Those three numbers are the whole family.
HOW THE GOLDENS WERE DERIVED, because it is what makes these vectors RED ON
ARRIVAL rather than a port agreeing with itself. Under the PRE-RULING code
`offset` was the literal distance a paste travelled, so a throwaway
derivation fixture pasting the same payload at EXPLICIT offsets 24 / 48 / 72
produced exactly the documents cumulative stacking must produce from
REPEATED base-24 pastes. Those documents are these goldens. The vectors
below then ask for the same documents from a DIFFERENT op sequence — the
repeated base-24 one — which is the sequence that did not work. The
derivation fixture is deleted; re-derive by writing it again.
THE FOUR DECISIONS the spec sentence leaves open, each pinned by a vector
here and written as artist-facing prose in workspace/actions.yaml:
1. RESET IS KEYED TO WHAT IS PASTED, not to a copy hook. A payload that
differs from the one the run is counting starts a new run at the base
step — so a copy of DIFFERENT artwork resets the offset, including an
EXTERNAL copy from another application that no in-app hook could see,
and a copy of the SAME artwork does not, because the first slot is
already occupied. A selection-keyed reset was rejected with a proof:
paste SETS the selection, so it could never reach step two.
2. `paste_in_place` DOES NOT PARTICIPATE. It neither advances the run nor
restarts it: 24, 0, 48.
3. `paste_preserving_layers` SHARES THE ONE RUN. The two commands differ
in WHICH LAYER artwork lands in, never in the offset.
4. A PASTE THAT LANDS NOTHING DOES NOT ADVANCE THE RUN.
THE PAYLOAD IS THE KEY, and it is the RAW STRING — the `text` the port read
off the system clipboard, or the `svg` fragment markup. Two consequences
worth stating: markup that differs only in whitespace is a DIFFERENT payload
and restarts the run, and the run is a SINGLE SLOT, so copying B between two
pastes of A loses A's count and the next A lands back on the first one.
Both are conservative and both are banked, not ruled.
WHAT THIS FAMILY CANNOT REACH, stated rather than implied: UNDO. The
operations runner applies `history` AFTER every transaction, so no fixture
can paste after an undo, and an embedded undo op inside a txn would desync
the checkpoint_equivalence gate (which replays journal[0..head] and never
replays history navigation). Undo/redo restoring the run is pinned by TWIN
PER-PORT probes instead — jas_dioxus op_apply::paste_stacking_tests and
JasSwift PasteStackingTests — over identical vectors. That is a weaker watch
than a shared golden and is named as such.
name: paste_stacking_family_setup_is_two_named_layers_background_and_foreground

_doc: THE HEADLINE REQUIREMENT. The same payload pasted twice at base 24 lands
at 36 and then 60. Before the fix both landed at 36 — one rect exactly
on top of the other, which reads on screen as a paste that did nothing.
name: paste_twice_stacks_24_then_48

_doc: The run is CUMULATIVE, not a one-shot doubling. A third paste must land
at 84, which separates 'multiply by the run position' from 'add 24 once
more if this is not the first paste' — a mutation that satisfies the
two-paste case with a fixed second step fails here.
name: paste_three_times_stacks_24_48_72

_doc: DECISION 1 — reset is keyed to WHAT IS PASTED. Two pastes of payload A
(36, 60), then two of a DIFFERENT payload B, which must restart at the
base step: B's rect sits at (24,0) in document space, so it lands at
(48,24) and then (72,48). This is what makes an EXTERNAL copy reset the
run without the paste path owning a copy hook.
name: paste_a_new_payload_restarts_the_stack

_doc: DECISION 2 — `paste_in_place` neither advances the run nor restarts it.
Interleaved between two ordinary pastes it lands on the source (12,12)
and the paste after it lands at 60, NOT back at 36 (which a reset would
give) and NOT at 84 (which participation would give). Three outcomes,
one vector, so no mutation satisfies it by accident.
name: paste_in_place_neither_advances_nor_resets_the_stack

_doc: DECISION 3 — 'Paste, Preserving Layers' shares the ONE run. Plain Paste
then preserving-layers over the SAME payload: the fragment layer is
unnamed, so preserve mode degenerates to plain Paste and the geometry is
byte-identical to `paste_twice_stacks_24_then_48`. Pinned BY FILE
IDENTITY — this vector points at that vector's own golden — so a second
run behind `preserve_layers` could not stay agreeing with it.
name: paste_preserving_layers_shares_the_one_stack

_doc: Decision 3 again, on the branch where R3 actually bites: a NAMED
fragment layer. The first preserving paste CREATES layer 'Imported' and
lands its child at 36; the second MATCHES that layer and appends at 60.
So the run advances across a layer creation, and the offset is not
quietly re-based when the target layer changes.
name: paste_preserving_named_layer_stacks_in_the_created_layer

_doc: THE PRODUCTION PATH. `text` carries the RAW CLIPBOARD PAYLOAD (D4/D5),
which is what BOTH ports' real paste actually reads — the `svg` param is
corpus-only. A non-SVG payload becomes a Text element at (offset,
offset+16), so two pastes put it at (24,40) and (48,64). Without this
vector the run could be implemented on the `svg` param alone and every
other case here would still pass while production pasted on one spot.
name: paste_clipboard_text_payload_stacks_too

_doc: DECISION 4 — a paste that lands NOTHING does not advance the run. The
empty string is a readable-but-empty clipboard (D5), a no-op; the paste
after it must still be the SECOND of the run at 60, not the third at 84.
Pinned by file identity against `paste_twice_stacks_24_then_48`.
name: a_paste_that_lands_nothing_does_not_advance_the_stack
